title: What If You Stood at the Coldest Spot Ever Measured?

scenes.text: What if you stood where Earth recorded its coldest air? A freezer would feel warm.
On July 21, 1983, Vostok Station in Antarctica hit minus 89.2 degrees Celsius, or minus 128.6 Fahrenheit.
The station sits on a plateau about 3,500 meters above sea level, roughly 1,300 kilometers from the South Pole.
In that cold, metal turns brittle, diesel fuel thickens, and your breath freezes into ice crystals almost instantly.
Any exposed skin would be in serious danger within moments.
And that is only the air. In 2013, satellites spotted snow on that plateau that may have dropped to minus 93 Celsius.

description:
What if you stood at the coldest air temperature ever measured on Earth?
Vostok Station in Antarctica recorded minus 89.2 degrees Celsius in 1983, and satellites later found snow that may have been even colder.
